claims.statement: `App` composes the SPA's providers as AuthProvider -> QueryClientProvider -> BrowserRouter -> AppRoutes with `<Toaster />` as a sibling of the router inside the query provider and `StrictMode` applied in `main.tsx`; the single module-level `queryClient` (defaults `staleTime: 30_000`, `retry: 1`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`) therefore survives client-side navigation and auth state is available to every descendant including the router guard.

`AppRoutes` declares `/login` as the only route outside the auth guard; every other path (`index`, `/routes`, `/routes/:routeId`, `/fares`, `/export`, `*`) nests inside a pathless `RequireAuth` layout route containing a pathless `AppShell` layout route, so an unknown URL is redirected to login before `NotFound` can render, the login screen renders without shell chrome, and `/login` has no authenticated-to-home redirect of its own.

`RequireAuth` is a four-branch gate over `useAuth()` status: `loading` renders a full-height spinner, `unreachable` renders `BackendUnreachable`, every other non-authenticated status renders `<Navigate to="/login" replace>` with `{ returnTo, sessionExpired }` in location state, and `authenticated` renders the shell `Outlet` — so an unreachable backend is never presented as an expired session and the guarded tree is unmounted in the other three branches.

Mid-use token expiry reaches the guard through a listener rather than a router event: the axios response interceptor saves the current path, clears the stored token and emits `sessionExpired`; `AuthProvider` then sets `status` to `unauthenticated` with that flag, and `RequireAuth` redirects to `/login` carrying both `returnTo` and the flag.

`features/auth/redirect.ts` is the guard's redirect-state contract: `getReturnPath` accepts only strings starting with `/` and not `//` (rejecting external and protocol-relative targets) and `getSessionExpired` accepts only a literal `true`; a `sessionStorage` copy of the return path survives a full reload and takes precedence over `location.state` when `Login` navigates back after a successful sign-in.

`BackendUnreachable` renders a branded plate whose single Retry button calls `AuthProvider.retry()`, re-running the session restore and disabling itself while `retrying`; the stored session is deliberately left intact so a retry or a later reload can resume without signing in again, because the token is only dropped for an actual UNAUTHORIZED response.

`lib/sections.ts` is the single registry of the four top-level sections (`overview`, `routes`, `fares`, `export`) with label, path and icon in rail order, and `getSectionByPath` resolves a section by exact path or by prefix followed by `/` — so `/routes/:routeId` keeps the Routes section active while the `/` entry only ever matches the exact root path and unknown paths resolve to `undefined`.

Extending navigation means touching two places: a new section is one `sections` entry plus one `<Route>` inside the `AppShell` layout route (the rail item, active state and header title follow from the registry), while a public route must instead be declared as a sibling of the `RequireAuth` layout route.

`NavRail` does not render the `Sidebar` primitive (which emits an in-flow `sidebar-gap` plus a `fixed` container); it renders its own absolutely positioned, full-height rail root carrying `role="navigation"`, `aria-label="Primary"`, `data-slot="sidebar"`/`data-state`/`data-collapsible`, `absolute inset-y-0 left-0 z-30` and `hidden md:flex`, composing only the primitive's sub-components and reading `state` from `useSidebar()`.

`AppShell` derives the rail's open state and the content padding from the mode: `expanded` forces `open` true and pads the content by the full rail width, `collapsed` forces `open` false and pads by icon width, and `hover` uses local hover state while the content keeps icon-width padding — so hover-expansion overlays the page at z-30 and never reflows or resizes the content, the 2026-08-16 reversal of ADR-0014's original always-push rail that the code marks as superseding D1 in ADR-0014.

Because `AppShell` controls the provider (`onOpenChange` honours a value only in `hover` mode), the stock `SidebarProvider` affordances are inert here: the `sidebar_state` cookie it writes on every `setOpen` is never read by any code and never rehydrates `open`, and its Cmd/Ctrl+B toggle only has an effect in `hover` mode.

The rail footer hosts the rail's mode control: a ghost icon button labelled "Sidebar visibility options" opens a radio-group dropdown titled "Sidebar control" with Expanded / Collapsed / Expand on hover, and each selection writes `setSidebarMode` then closes the menu explicitly because radio items do not auto-close.

`uiStore` is a plain in-memory zustand store whose `sidebarMode` defaults to `expanded` and which has no `persist` middleware, so the chosen mode survives client-side navigation but resets on a full page reload; ADR-0014's "persisted `sidebarMode`" wording refers to the user's mode being read as-is and never forced per route rather than to browser persistence.

The rail's width tokens come from `SidebarProvider`'s inline style — `--sidebar-width: 16rem` (256 px) and `--sidebar-width-icon: 3rem` (48 px) — not from application CSS, which is why the rail and the workspace geometry share those two figures.

The collapsed rail stays labelled: `BrandMark compact={collapsed}` fades the wordmark out and switches the image `alt` to "Komyuter", and every menu button passes a `tooltip` that the primitive reveals only while the rail is collapsed and not on mobile.

`Header` derives its title from `getSectionByPath(pathname)`, with a `routes` special case that reads the workspace's `routeId` from `usePlottingStore` and calls `useRouteQuery(routeId)` to render `Route › {name}` (showing `…` while the detail loads) or `Route` when nothing is open, falling back to `Komyuter` for unknown paths; the `<h1>` carries `aria-live="polite"`.

The header's Sign Out runs `signOut()`, toasts "Signed out" and replaces navigation to `/login`; `signOut()` clears the stored token and auth state without any request, so the shell never calls the server's idempotent `POST /api/auth/logout` (which performs a global Supabase sign-out) even though `docs/ADMIN.md` describes admin sign-out as that call — revocation of an issued token therefore depends on its expiry.

`AppShell` renders a `h-svh` flex column (skip link, ConnectionBanner, rail plus `SidebarInset`) in which the window never scrolls: `Header` is a fixed `h-14 shrink-0` strip outside the scroll container and `#main-content` (`min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-auto`, `tabIndex={-1}`) is the only scroll region hosting the route `Outlet`, so pages must be `h-full` to fill the viewport.

The accessibility scaffolding of the shell is a `sr-only`-until-focused "Skip to content" link targeting the programmatically focusable `#main-content` (`tabIndex={-1}`), the rail exposed as the `role="navigation"` landmark `aria-label="Primary"`, and `SidebarInset` as the `<main>` landmark.

`useOnline` seeds from `navigator.onLine` and subscribes to the browser `online`/`offline` events; `ConnectionBanner` renders nothing while online and, while offline, a full-width `role="status"` warning bar above the rail/content row that merely reports the state (no queueing or retry) and is shared by the shell and the login screen.

`NarrowWindowGate` self-measures its wrapper with a `ResizeObserver` in a layout effect and tracks the viewport floor with a `matchMedia("(min-width: 1024px)")` listener, then blocks when the window is below that floor or when `computeMapWidth(width, 0, mode)` falls under `minMapWidth` (400 px); while the measured width is still 0 it renders the children so the plate never flashes on first paint.

When blocked, the gate paints an opaque `absolute inset-0 z-50` plate carrying `role="status" aria-live="polite"` copy that asks for a wider window or a collapsed navigation rail, keeps the children (including the MapLibre canvas) mounted underneath, and sets `inert` on the covered chrome through the DOM property in a layout effect so the covered panels cannot be focused or clicked; it is mounted by `RouteWorkspace` inside `MapProvider` but outside `RouteMap`, so gating never touches the GL instance.

Because `AppShell` pads the content rather than inserting a spacer, the gate's measured wrapper already excludes the rail and the gate passes `railW = 0`; at a literal 1024 px window the 48 px collapsed rail leaves 976 px of workspace where `focus`/`edit` computes 384 px and the plate appears while `overview` computes 768 px and passes, so the effective floor is roughly 1024 px of workspace and an expanded 256 px rail (208 px wider) can trip the invariant in a window that passes while collapsed.

The declared 1024 px viewport floor is a string literal inside `NarrowWindowGate`'s `matchMedia` query rather than a token in `WORKSPACE_GEOMETRY` (which holds only `leftCol`, `rightCol`, `gutter` and `minMapWidth`), so changing the desktop floor requires editing the gate.

The content padding that encodes the rail width is animated (`transition-[padding] duration-150 ease-linear`) on `SidebarInset` while the gate re-measures on every resize, so a rail toggle re-evaluates the gate as the width animates and can show or hide the plate during the transition.

The gate is mounted only by the workspace route: `Overview`, `Fares` and `Export` render as ordinary pages under the shell with no width gate, so the desktop floor is enforced for the fixed-plate workspace rather than for the whole shell.

All route components are statically imported by the router: there is no lazy route loading, no `<Suspense>` boundary and no error boundary in the app, so a matched route renders in the same commit as its shell. `BrowserRouter` is used with no `basename` and no hash fallback, so root-absolute section paths require the host to serve `index.html` for unknown paths for deep links to work.

`apps/admin`'s vitest setup runs node-environment tests restricted to `src/tests/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}` (invoked as `pnpm --filter admin test`), and the shell's pure dependencies are covered there — the sections registry and path resolution, redirect-state sanitization, and the workspace geometry/gate arithmetic — while `AppShell`, `NavRail`, `Header` and `NarrowWindowGate` have no component or DOM tests, leaving the rail modes and the gate plate to manual verification.
